translations.text: "This is the Christ." Others said: "No, rather he is leading the people astray. Is the Christ to come from Galilee?
Does not the Scripture say, 'From the line of David and from the village of Bethlehem'?" And again others said: "When the Christ comes, no one will know where he is from."
Commentary: Their minds were divided in all sorts of ways, as happens with a disorderly crowd. They were not listening properly to what was said, in a way that would let them understand it properly.
That is why the Lord gave these people no answer, even though they were saying, "Is the Christ to come from Galilee?"
Nathanael, however, spoke more harshly and more [?] when he said, "Can anything good come out of Nazareth?"
Yet the Saviour praised him all the more, as a true Israelite. These people, by contrast, said to Nicodemus:
"Search and see: no prophet has arisen out of Galilee."
They did not say this in order to learn and come to know the truth. They said it only to discredit the cause of Christ.
Nathanael, however, was a lover of truth and had learned all the Scriptures well.
That is why he spoke those words. These people, though, were concerned with one thing only: that no one should think of him that he is the Christ.
For this reason he revealed nothing to them, because they were even contradicting themselves. At one point they say:
"We know where he is from," and at another point, "He comes from Bethlehem." It is clear that they knew and still opposed him, for:
Look, let us grant that they did not know the place, because he was brought up in Nazareth.
That is impossible too, since it was well known that he had not been born there. But let us grant that they did not know.
Did they not know his lineage either? He was of the seed and lineage of David. How then could they say, "Is he not of David's lineage?"
No, they said all this out of their wickedness, so as to hide the truth. Why did they not come to him and say:
"Everything you do amazes us. But you command us to believe everything as the Scripture says. So tell us: how can this be?
For it is written, 'The Christ comes from Bethlehem,' and you have come from Galilee?"
But they said nothing of the kind to him. Everything they said, they said out of wickedness. So that you may know they were not speaking those words in order to learn the truth, the Evangelist said:
Gospel: "Some of them wanted to seize him, but no one laid hands on him."
Commentary: Even if there had been nothing else, this alone should have been enough to soften their hearts. But their hearts were not softened, and they did not repent either. As it is written:
"They were scattered and did not repent." For such is wickedness: it is willing to obey no one and to yield to no one.
It is eager for one thing only: to carry out its own evil and to kill the one against whom it has plotted evil.
But hear what Scripture says: "Whoever digs a pit for his neighbour will fall into it himself." This is what happened to them as well.
They wanted to kill him so that his preaching would be extinguished, but the opposite happened. That grace shines by the grace of Christ,
For these Jews also wanted to hide it, and they acted as though they were willingly eager to make it known. First they asked him: "How were your eyes opened?"
They did this so that they could accuse him of some evil, as they did in another place. Since they had nothing to say, they said:
"He casts out demons by Beelzebul." And here too, since they had nothing to say, they said: "He breaks the Sabbath," and again, "He is a sinner."
O you blinded ones! When you were inflamed with anger, did he not ask all of you together: "Which of you convicts me of sin?"
And since none of you could say anything, he refuted you. For if you had had anything to say, you would not have kept silent, you who heard something such as:
"He is before Abraham," and you wanted to stone him. And it was said: "He is not from God."
And you named yourselves as belonging to God, you murderers, and to him who had done so many signs you said: "He is not from God."
If you had had even a shadow of a fault to charge him with, you would not have kept silent.
But when they could not make this accusation about the Sabbath stand, and were weakened on every side, they then turned to another wickedness and devised something worse and more senseless, that is:
"They did not believe that he had been blind and had received his sight." But from what they said, "He does not keep the Sabbath," it is clear that
they did believe, and all the believers and those who knew were speaking about him. But, as I have said, falsehood always harms itself and cannot hide the truth;
instead it makes the truth shine out all the more, as happened now. So that no one could say, "Perhaps it was not he?",
the matter was made plain for this reason by the very summoning of his parents, which was meant to hide it. For the parents acknowledged that he was their son who had been blind.
Since they could not frighten him, and he preached boldly, they then wanted to discredit the miracle through his parents. And see the wickedness of their questioning:
they set them in their midst in order to frighten them, and began to question them angrily:
Gospel: "Is this your son, of whom you say that he was born blind?"
Commentary: They did not say, "who was once blind," but "of whom you say that he was born blind."
They questioned them like this, with malice and wickedness. O you defiled and utterly foul ones!
What father would want to say such a thing falsely about his own son? For [they meant]: "You say it. If he is blind, how does he now see?"
O this folly! [They meant]: "You have told this story falsely." For by these two points they wanted to bring them to denial: first, because "you say that
he was born blind," and second, "how then does he now see?" So three questions were put:
first, whether he was their son; second, whether he was born blind; and third, about his gaining sight. They acknowledged the first two and kept silent about the third.
This too happened for the sake of greater truth, so that no one else, but the healed man himself, as the most trustworthy witness, would confess the matter.
For how would the parents have said anything false, when out of fear of the Jews they kept silent even about the truth, and said:
For since they called themselves worshippers of God, he added [?] and said: "and does his will."

For this alone is not enough, that a person should know God. Then: "You who question me idly and in vain, and do not seek to hear for the sake of the truth, but only so that you may refute what has been said."
Gospel: "Or do you also want to become his disciples?"
Commentary: See, he has now placed himself in the company of his disciples, for he says, "Do you also?"
This shows that he had made himself his disciple, and he rebuked them and wounded them.
And he strikes them all the harder, for this is the act of a soul made bold, soaring, and scornful of [?], which showed his great esteem for him and indicated
that they were vainly reviling so wonderful and true a Christ, and that he suffers nothing from their contempt. He raises the level of what he says:
Gospel: "Never since the world began has it been heard that anyone opened the eyes of someone born blind." That is, he means, it is well known
that God does not listen to sinners. But this man has not only performed a miracle, but a miracle of a kind that no human being has ever done.
And therefore it is clear that he surpassed everyone in virtue, and his work is above that of all people. But listen to what they said:
Gospel: "You were born entirely in sin, and are you teaching us?" And they drove him out.
Commentary: For as long as they expected that he would deny it, they kept calling him and treated him as trustworthy. But if he was not trustworthy, why did they question him twice?
But since he spoke the truth fearlessly, at the very moment when they should have marvelled all the more at what had been done, they condemned him all the more.
But what does this saying mean: "You were born entirely in sin"?
For here they maliciously reproach him even for his blindness, and claimed that he was born blind because of sins, which was impossible.
And that is why Christ said: "I came into this world for judgment, so that those who do not see may see, and those who see may become blind."
Gospel: "You were born entirely in sin, and are you teaching us?"
Commentary: And what did the man say? He did not lay down a rule of his own. Instead he stated something known to everyone:
"We know that God does not listen to sinners." And they drove him out. See this herald of the truth, how his poverty was no obstacle to wisdom.
Do you see how much they said to him, and how he bore witness to the truth by deed and by word?
Teaching 58 [ნჱ]: That we must learn from the holy Scriptures and turn away from evil sights. All this is written so that we may imitate it.
For if a poor and blind man, who had not even seen him, showed such boldness and stood up against all of them,
frenzied men and demons as they were, and chose to be cast out rather than to trample on the truth,
how much more is it fitting for us, who have spent so long in the faith and have seen so many miracles,
to whom a greater good has been given than to him, and whose inner eyes have been opened,
to whom belong glory and might, together with the Father and the Holy Spirit, now and always and forever and ever. Amen.

And hear the prophet, how he says: "My wounds stink and are rotten."
But you ask the Lord in words to forget your sins, yet by your deeds you do not let him forget them; instead you remind him of them every day,
for you lay the gains of wickedness on the altar and give them to the saints. Or do you say:
"I am not giving what was stolen, but something else, which was my own"?
And do you not understand that, even if only a little gained by lawlessness falls into a great amount of wealth,
it defiles all of it, just as a little dung muddies a pure spring and makes it stink?
We wash our hands when we go to church, but not our hearts, and we do not know that it is not the hands that say anything,
but the soul that makes supplications to God. So we hurry to do worthless and small things and disregard the great ones.
For if praying with unwashed hands is improper, is not praying with a defiled soul much more evil?
For this reason the Jews too were given over to evil deeds, yet were eager to wash their hands with water.
For this reason Scripture says to them: "Wash your soul clean of wickedness; how long will foul thoughts remain with you?"
So let us wash ourselves, not with mud but with the water of almsgiving, and not with greed. First keep away from plunder and robbery, and then give alms.
Turn away from evil and do good. Hold your hands back from plunder, and in this way direct them to almsgiving.
If we clothe some people with the same hands we use to strip others, this is abominable before the Lord. For it would have been better for Cain too
if he had not offered anything. And if the one who offered what was inferior angered God, will not the one who offers what belongs to another anger him far more?
For he will say to you: "I did not teach you robbery, and you honor me with what was stolen?
Do you really think, lawless one, that I am like you? Now I will rebuke you and set your sins before your face."
But may none of us ever hear this voice. Instead, may we give pure alms and inherit the eternal good things by the grace and love for humankind of our Lord Jesus Christ,
to whom belong glory and might, together with the Father and the Holy Spirit, now and always and forever and ever. Amen.

But as I see it, this saying fits not only that city but also those

And so in the evening he stood before them as they sat inside behind shut doors. He did not knock at the door, nor did he make any commotion,
but in an instant he stood before them and showed them his hands and his side. With words, too, he calmed their troubled minds, saying to them:
"Peace be with you", which means "Do not be troubled". And he reminded them of the word that he had spoken to them before the crucifixion:
"My peace I leave with you." And again: "In me may you have peace."
Gospel: The disciples rejoiced when they saw the Lord.
Commentary: Do you see how words are fulfilled in deeds?
For what he had said to them before the crucifixion, "I will see you, and your hearts will rejoice, and no one will take your joy from you", has now been fulfilled in deed.
Since they were engaged in an unending war with the Jews, he says to them again and again:
"Peace be with you", so that he might give them peace as a means of overcoming that war and as a consolation. For he had said this word first of all, as soon as he rose.
For this reason the apostle Paul always says, "Grace and peace to you." But to the women the Lord announced joy first of all,
for that sex was in sorrow. So, to suit the men's warfare, he announced peace,
but because of the women's sorrow he announced joy. And since he had accomplished everything, he now speaks of the work of the cross: "Peace be with you!"
Since every obstacle had been removed and the victory had become glorious, he then said to them:
Gospel: "As the Father has sent me, so I also send you."
Commentary: That is: "There is no longer any difficulty before you, since I have conquered, and I am sending you."
At this point he gladdens their souls and makes them joyful, when they heard that they were to do the work of the Lord himself.
He no longer prays to the Father, but by his own authority gives them grace and power. For the evangelist says:
Gospel: And when he had said this, he breathed on them and said: "Receive the Holy Spirit. If you forgive the sins of any, they are forgiven; and if you retain the sins of any, they are retained."
Commentary: When a king sends out his governors, he gives them authority to cast into prison and to release.
In the same way, when the Lord sent out the disciples, he gave them this kind of authority. But how?
For he had said earlier, "If I do not go away, he will not come," and yet here he now gives the Spirit. Some say:
"He did not give the Holy Spirit, but by that breathing he made them ready and fit to receive him when he came." For if Daniel, when he saw an angel,
was struck with terror and became afraid, how could they have borne that awesome grace if they had not been prepared beforehand?
That is why he did not say, "You have received the Holy Spirit," but "Receive the Holy Spirit." Yet it is also not unfitting for us to say:
